questions.correctAnswer: The Earth's land, water, people, and how they interact
distractors: Only the names of capital cities
The stars and planets in outer space
questions.explanation: Geography is the study of Earth's physical features, its people, and the connections between them.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Geographers connect land and people.
questions.question: What do geographers study?

questions.correctAnswer: Pinpointing the exact location of a place on Earth
distractors: Measuring how deep an ocean is
questions.explanation: Latitude and longitude form a grid of imaginary lines that gives every place on Earth an exact address.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Latitude and longitude are Earth's address system.
questions.question: What are latitude and longitude used for?

questions.correctAnswer: The Northern and Southern Hemispheres
questions.explanation: The equator is an imaginary line around Earth's middle. Places north of it are in the Northern Hemisphere and places south of it are in the Southern Hemisphere.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The equator is Earth's belt between north and south.
questions.question: The equator divides Earth into which two halves?

questions.correctAnswer: Latin America, where Spanish and Portuguese are widely spoken
questions.explanation: A cultural region is defined by shared human features such as language or religion, not by landforms or water.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Shared language can draw the borders of a cultural region.
questions.question: Which of these is an example of a cultural region?

questions.correctAnswer: To organize and compare places that share features
distractors: To make maps as small as possible
questions.explanation: Regions help geographers organize a huge world into areas with common features so the areas can be studied and compared.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Regions sort the world into study-sized pieces.
questions.question: Why do geographers divide the world into regions?

questions.correctAnswer: Farmers building terraces on steep hillsides to grow crops
distractors: A volcano erupting on an island
A river slowly cutting a canyon
questions.explanation: Human-environment interaction means people and nature affecting each other. Building terraces changes the land so people can farm it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Terraces show people shaping the land they live on.
questions.question: Which of these is an example of human-environment interaction?

questions.correctAnswer: Half of the Earth
distractors: The imaginary line around Earth's middle
questions.explanation: The word hemisphere means half of a sphere. Earth can be divided into Northern and Southern, or Eastern and Western, hemispheres.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Hemi means half - a hemisphere is half the Earth.
questions.question: What is a hemisphere?

questions.correctAnswer: The connection between physical features and where people settle
distractors: The history of ancient Egyptian kings
The trade routes of the Mediterranean Sea
questions.explanation: Almost all Egyptians live near the Nile because the river provides water in a desert land. Settlement follows physical features such as rivers.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: People settle where water and resources are found.
questions.question: A geographer studying why most Egyptians live along the Nile River is mainly studying which relationship?

questions.correctAnswer: A political map
questions.explanation: Political maps show human-made boundaries such as country borders, plus cities and capitals. Physical maps show landforms instead.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Political maps draw the borders people made.
questions.question: Which type of map would best show the borders of countries and their capital cities?

questions.correctAnswer: Differences in elevation and closeness to oceans
distractors: One city using a different calendar
The cities being ruled by different governments
questions.explanation: Latitude affects climate, but elevation and nearby oceans also matter. A high mountain city and a coastal city at the same latitude can feel very different.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Height and oceans can overrule latitude.
questions.question: Two cities sit at the same latitude but have very different climates. What could best explain this?

questions.correctAnswer: Erosion by wind and water
questions.explanation: Erosion happens when wind, water, or ice slowly carry away soil and rock, reshaping the land over long periods of time.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Wind and water patiently wear the land away.
questions.question: Which physical process wears away land over time?

questions.correctAnswer: Extreme heat and very little fresh water make life difficult
distractors: The land is covered by thick rainforest
Governments forbid people from living there
It is completely surrounded by ocean
questions.explanation: The Sahara is one of the hottest, driest places on Earth. Without reliable water, large populations cannot live there.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: No water, no crowd - deserts stay nearly empty.
questions.question: Why do very few people live in the central Sahara?

questions.correctAnswer: The average number of people living in a given area
distractors: The total land area of a country
How fast a city is growing
The number of babies born each year
questions.explanation: Population density compares how many people live in an area, such as per square mile. Cities have high density and open countryside has low density.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Density counts how crowded a place is.
questions.question: What is population density?

questions.correctAnswer: Good jobs and good schools
questions.explanation: Pull factors attract people to a new place, such as jobs and schools. Push factors like drought and war drive people away from a place.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Jobs and schools pull people in.
questions.question: Which of these is a pull factor that draws people to move to a new place?

questions.correctAnswer: Changing the environment to make farming possible
distractors: Being completely controlled by the environment
Moving away from all dry land
Giving up farming in dry areas
questions.explanation: People modify their environment to meet their needs. Irrigation brings water to dry land so crops can grow where they otherwise could not.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Irrigation rewrites dry land into farmland.
questions.question: A farmer in a dry region digs wells and builds irrigation channels to water crops. This is an example of people...

questions.correctAnswer: Water routes make trade and travel easier
distractors: People need to swim for exercise
Rivers keep cities cool in summer
questions.explanation: For centuries, ships were the cheapest way to move goods. Cities on coasts and rivers grew rich and large through trade.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Ports grow where the ships can go.
questions.question: Why are many of the world's biggest cities located on coasts or along rivers?

questions.correctAnswer: The growth of cities as people move there from rural areas
distractors: Planting trees in a city park
questions.explanation: Urbanization is the process of cities growing as more people move from farms and villages into urban areas, often for jobs.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Urbanization means the city keeps growing.
questions.question: What is urbanization?

questions.correctAnswer: Access to fresh water for drinking and farming
distractors: Being close to the tops of mountains
Living as far as possible from other people
Having large amounts of desert nearby
questions.explanation: The first farming villages grew beside rivers and lakes because people, animals, and crops all need fresh water to survive.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The first villages hugged the rivers.
questions.question: Which factor most influenced where early human settlements formed?

questions.correctAnswer: It is high, because rich soil supports farming and towns
distractors: It is low, because deltas are too dry for farming
It stays at zero because of flooding
It is the same as in the middle of a desert
questions.explanation: River deltas have rich, well-watered soil left by floods. That soil supports heavy farming, which feeds large, dense populations.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Fertile deltas feed crowds of people.
questions.question: What usually happens to population density near a fertile river delta?

questions.correctAnswer: Warm ocean currents carry heat toward Europe's coast
distractors: Europe is actually closer to the equator
Canada has no oceans anywhere near it
Europe's mountains block every cold wind
questions.explanation: Warm Atlantic currents flow toward Western Europe and soften its winters, even though it lies as far north as much colder parts of Canada.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The warm Atlantic gives Europe a softer winter.
questions.question: Why does Western Europe have milder winters than Canadian cities at about the same latitude?

questions.correctAnswer: Laws and a constitution that everyone, including leaders, must follow
questions.explanation: In a limited government, a constitution and laws set clear boundaries on what leaders may do, and leaders can be held to those rules.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: In limited government, even leaders follow the law.
questions.question: In a limited government, what limits the power of leaders?

questions.correctAnswer: Make decisions without being bound by laws or the consent of citizens
distractors: Be removed by voters whenever citizens wish
Share power equally with all citizens
questions.explanation: Unlimited governments place no real legal limits on rulers. Citizens have few protected rights and little say in decisions.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Unlimited rulers answer to no one.
questions.question: In an unlimited government, leaders are able to...

questions.correctAnswer: A government where citizens hold the power and vote for their leaders
distractors: Rule by one king for his whole life
A country with no government at all
questions.explanation: In a democracy, power comes from the people. Citizens vote in elections to choose leaders and shape laws.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Democracy means the people hold the power.
questions.question: What is a democracy?

questions.correctAnswer: The monarch's power is limited by a constitution and elected lawmakers
distractors: There is no monarch at all
Citizens elect the monarch for life
The monarch is only an army general
questions.explanation: A constitutional monarch must share power with an elected government under a constitution. An absolute monarch rules with nearly total power.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A constitution puts a leash on the crown.
questions.question: How is a constitutional monarchy different from an absolute monarchy?

questions.correctAnswer: Direct democracy
questions.explanation: In a direct democracy, citizens themselves vote on each law. In a representative democracy, citizens elect officials to make laws for them.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Direct means the people vote on the laws themselves.
questions.question: Citizens in a country vote directly on every law instead of electing representatives to decide for them. This system is an example of...

questions.correctAnswer: Voting in elections and staying informed about issues
distractors: Obeying only the laws they personally like
Serving in the military for their whole life
questions.explanation: Democracies depend on active citizens. Voting, learning about issues, and taking part in the community keep the system working.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Good citizens show up and stay informed.
questions.question: Which of these is a responsibility of citizens in a democracy?

questions.correctAnswer: One leader who rules with total control
questions.explanation: A dictator seizes or holds total control over the government and often over daily life, without free elections or legal limits.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A dictator keeps all the power alone.
questions.question: Who holds the power in a dictatorship?

questions.correctAnswer: Theocracy
questions.explanation: A theocracy is governed by religious leaders, and its laws are based on religious teachings.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Theo means God - a theocracy is ruled by religious leaders.
questions.question: A country's government is run by religious leaders, and its laws are based on religious law. This system is called a...

questions.correctAnswer: So citizens can choose their leaders and replace them peacefully
distractors: To celebrate the founding of the country
Because leaders must serve for life
To let citizens vote on every single law
questions.explanation: Free and fair elections let citizens pick leaders and peacefully remove them, which keeps government accountable to the people.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Elections are democracy's peaceful reset button.
questions.question: Why do democracies hold free and fair elections?

questions.correctAnswer: Power is shared between a national government and state or provincial governments
distractors: One central government holds all the power
Every city governs itself with no national government
The military shares power with the citizens
questions.explanation: In a federal system, power is divided. The national government handles things like defense, while states or provinces handle local matters like schools.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Federal means power is shared, top to bottom.
questions.question: A federal system of government is one in which...

questions.correctAnswer: Businesses and consumers, through buying and selling
questions.explanation: In a market economy, businesses decide what to sell and consumers decide what to buy. Prices help guide those choices.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: In a market economy, shoppers help steer the ship.
questions.question: In a market economy, who mostly decides what goods are produced?

questions.correctAnswer: Owns most businesses and decides what will be produced
questions.explanation: In a command economy, the government controls the economy: it owns most factories and farms and decides what they produce.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: In a command economy, the government gives the orders.
questions.question: In a command economy, the government...

questions.correctAnswer: A mixed economy
questions.explanation: Nearly all modern economies are mixed: markets and private businesses do most of the work, while government provides services and sets some rules.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Mixed means markets plus some government.
questions.question: Most modern countries, including the United States, have which type of economy?

questions.correctAnswer: The price usually rises
questions.explanation: When many buyers chase few goods, sellers can charge more. High demand with low supply pushes prices up.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Everyone wants it, few exist - the price climbs.
questions.question: What usually happens to the price of a popular toy when demand is high but supply is low?

questions.correctAnswer: International trade and interdependence
distractors: Isolation from the rest of the world
A barter system inside one village
questions.explanation: Countries trade what they produce best and buy what they need. This mutual dependence is called interdependence.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Trade ties countries together like knots in a net.
questions.question: Country A sells coffee to Country B, and Country B sells cars to Country A. This is an example of...

questions.correctAnswer: The growing connection of countries through trade, technology, and culture
distractors: The study of globes and maps
A country closing all its borders
questions.explanation: Globalization means the world is increasingly connected. Goods, money, ideas, and culture move between countries faster than ever.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Globalization shrinks the world into one neighborhood.
questions.question: What is globalization?

questions.correctAnswer: The language people speak
questions.explanation: Culture is the way of life of a group of people. Its elements include language, religion, customs, foods, clothing, and the arts.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Culture is how a people lives, speaks, and celebrates.
questions.question: Which of these is an element of culture?

questions.correctAnswer: Islam
questions.explanation: Islam began in Southwest Asia in the 600s CE. Its followers, called Muslims, read the Quran, and Islam is one of the world's largest religions.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The Quran is the holy book of Islam.
questions.question: Which religion began in Southwest Asia, is followed by about two billion people worldwide, and has the Quran as its holy book?

questions.correctAnswer: Cultural diffusion
questions.explanation: Cultural diffusion is the spread of ideas, customs, and goods from one culture to another, often through migration, trade, and travel.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: When people move, their customs travel with them.
questions.question: A tradition spreads from one culture to another as people migrate and share their customs, and over time both cultures change. Geographers call this process...

questions.correctAnswer: Developed countries generally have higher incomes and better access to healthcare, education, and services
distractors: Developed countries always have larger land areas
Developing countries have no cities at all
Standard of living depends only on climate
questions.explanation: Standard of living measures how well people live. Developed countries tend to offer higher incomes and stronger schools, hospitals, and services.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Standard of living shows how well daily life works.
questions.question: Why does standard of living differ between developed and developing countries?

questions.correctAnswer: A federal republic where citizens elect representatives
distractors: A direct democracy where everyone votes on each law
questions.explanation: The United States is a republic, so citizens elect representatives, and it is federal, so power is shared between the national and state governments.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The US elects its leaders and shares power with states.
questions.question: The government of the United States is best described as...

questions.correctAnswer: Power is shared between national and state governments, and citizens elect their leaders
distractors: Each state is a fully independent country
Citizens vote directly on every single law
questions.explanation: Federal describes the sharing of power between levels of government, and republic describes a system where citizens elect representatives to govern.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Federal shares power; republic elects leaders.
questions.question: Why is the United States called a federal republic?

questions.correctAnswer: A parliamentary democracy and constitutional monarchy
questions.explanation: Canada's elected Parliament governs the country, while the monarch serves as head of state with powers limited by the constitution.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Canada pairs a parliament with a limited crown.
questions.question: What type of government does Canada have?

questions.correctAnswer: English and French settlers both shaped the country, and French is widely spoken, especially in Quebec
distractors: Canadians voted to have three official languages
French is spoken in only one small town
The United States required Canada to do it
questions.explanation: Both Britain and France colonized Canada. Today English and French are official languages, and Quebec is a mainly French-speaking province.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Two founding peoples, two official languages.
questions.question: Why does Canada have two official languages, English and French?

questions.correctAnswer: Huge forests, minerals, and freshwater lakes support industries like timber and mining, while the cold climate limits farming mostly to the south
distractors: Canada's warm tropical climate makes it a top coffee producer
Canada has almost no natural resources to trade
Mountains cover the entire country, so no farming is possible
questions.explanation: Canada's natural wealth includes forests, minerals, energy, and the Great Lakes, but its northern cold keeps most farming in southern areas.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Canada's riches grow in forests and hide in rock.
questions.question: How has geography shaped Canada's economy?

questions.correctAnswer: In the southern part of the country, close to the United States border
distractors: In the far northern Arctic regions
Spread perfectly evenly across the whole country
questions.explanation: Southern Canada has a milder climate and holds the major cities, farms, and industries, so most Canadians live near the US border.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Canadians cluster where the winters soften.
questions.question: Where do most Canadians live?

questions.correctAnswer: Mexican dishes such as tacos and burritos are common in restaurants and homes
distractors: Sushi is the main food of the Southwest
No foods from other cultures are eaten there
Only seafood from the Atlantic Ocean is served
questions.explanation: The Southwest shares a long border and history with Mexico. Migration and cultural diffusion made Mexican food a daily part of life there.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Borderlands blend flavors from both sides.
questions.question: Which of these shows the influence of Mexican culture in the southwestern United States?

questions.correctAnswer: Warm climate, growing job markets, and air conditioning made hot southern cities attractive and comfortable to live in
distractors: Those cities are the oldest in the United States
The government forced people to move there
The cities gave free land to everyone who arrived
questions.explanation: Sun Belt cities boomed as businesses created jobs in warm regions, and air conditioning made hot summers comfortable for large populations.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Sunshine plus jobs pulled people south and west.
questions.question: Why have large numbers of people moved to Sun Belt cities such as Phoenix and Houston in recent decades?

questions.correctAnswer: Lakes and connecting waterways provided cheap transportation for heavy goods and resources
distractors: The region has the warmest climate in North America
Gold was discovered under the lakes
No other region wanted any factories
questions.explanation: The Great Lakes and canals let ships move iron, grain, and factory goods cheaply, so industry grew along their shores in both countries.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Cheap shipping built the Great Lakes factory belt.
questions.question: The Great Lakes region of the United States and Canada became a major industrial center mainly because...

questions.correctAnswer: The United States, Mexico, and Canada
distractors: The United States, Brazil, and Canada
The United States, Mexico, and Spain
questions.explanation: The USMCA is a trade agreement between the three North American neighbors: the United States, Mexico, and Canada.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: USMCA - the US, Mexico, and Canada trade as neighbors.
questions.question: The USMCA trade agreement connects which three countries?

questions.correctAnswer: Spain and Portugal colonized the region centuries ago
distractors: Those languages first began in Latin America
Trade with Asia spread the languages
Everyone chose them in a recent vote
questions.explanation: Spanish and Portuguese settlers ruled most of Latin America for about 300 years, and their languages became the region's main languages.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Empires leave their languages behind.
questions.question: Why do most people in Latin America speak Spanish or Portuguese?

questions.correctAnswer: Find jobs and better services in the capital city
distractors: Farm rich soil in the downtown area
questions.explanation: Like capitals everywhere, Mexico City pulls migrants from rural areas who are looking for work, schools, hospitals, and other services.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Capitals pull people in with jobs and services.
questions.question: Many Mexicans move from rural areas to Mexico City mainly to...

questions.correctAnswer: Roman Catholic Christianity
questions.explanation: Spanish and Portuguese colonizers brought Roman Catholic Christianity, which remains the largest religion in most Latin American countries.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Catholic cathedrals anchor Latin America's plazas.
questions.question: Which religion is most widely practiced in Latin America?

questions.correctAnswer: Portuguese
questions.explanation: Portugal, not Spain, colonized Brazil. That is why Brazilians speak Portuguese while most of their neighbors speak Spanish.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Brazil is the Portuguese-speaking giant.
questions.question: Brazil is different from most of Latin America because its main language is...

questions.correctAnswer: Its trees absorb carbon and produce oxygen, but clearing land for farms and ranches is destroying large areas of it
distractors: It produces most of the world's drinking water and is fully protected
It is the world's largest desert and it keeps growing
Its trees are cut for paper but replanting is forbidden
questions.explanation: The Amazon stores enormous amounts of carbon and supports unmatched wildlife, but deforestation for cattle ranches and farms threatens it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The Amazon breathes for the whole planet.
questions.question: Why is the Amazon rainforest so important to the whole world, and why is it threatened?

questions.correctAnswer: It lets ships travel between the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans without sailing all the way around South America
distractors: It connects the Panama River to the Amazon River
It provides drinking water to all of Central America
It blocks ships from entering the Caribbean Sea
questions.explanation: The Panama Canal cuts across Central America, saving ships a long, dangerous trip around the southern tip of South America.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The canal is the world's greatest shortcut.
questions.question: The Panama Canal is important to world trade because it...

questions.correctAnswer: An agricultural export that earns money through trade
distractors: A product that cannot be sold to anyone
A food that is only eaten locally
A mineral dug from deep mines
questions.explanation: Coffee is grown in Latin America's highlands and sold around the world, making it an important export crop for countries like Colombia and Brazil.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Highland coffee travels the world.
questions.question: Coffee grown in the highlands of Colombia and Brazil is an example of...

questions.correctAnswer: It blended European language and religion with Native American and African cultures
distractors: It had almost no effect on daily life
It made every country exactly like Spain
questions.explanation: Latin American culture today is a blend: Spanish and Portuguese language and Catholic faith mixed with Native traditions and African influences.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Three roots grew into one blended culture.
questions.question: How did Spanish colonization most change the cultures of Latin America?

questions.correctAnswer: Terraces create flat planting steps and hold soil and water on steep slopes
distractors: Terraces keep wild animals away from villages
Flat land is forbidden in the mountains
Terraces make crops grow during winter
questions.explanation: Mountain farmers cut flat steps into slopes. Terraces keep soil and rainwater from washing away, making steep land farmable.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Terraces are staircases for crops.
questions.question: Why do many farmers in the Andes Mountains grow crops on steep terraces?

questions.correctAnswer: Tourism
questions.explanation: Many Caribbean islands have small land areas and few resources, so hotels, beaches, and visitors bring in most of their income through tourism.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Sun and sand pay the bills in the Caribbean.
questions.question: A Caribbean island country earns most of its money from visitors who come for its beaches and warm weather. This economy depends mainly on...

questions.correctAnswer: A group of European countries that cooperate on trade and laws
questions.explanation: The European Union is an alliance of member countries that work together on trade, laws, and travel while remaining separate nations.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The EU is a team of countries, not one country.
questions.question: What is the European Union (EU)?

questions.correctAnswer: Goods can move between members without extra border taxes, and many members share the euro currency
distractors: Members must stop trading with each other
Each member prints the money of the others
Members may sell goods only inside the EU
questions.explanation: The EU's single market removes tariffs between members, and most members use the euro, so buying and selling across borders is simpler.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: One market, shared money, easier trade.
questions.question: How does belonging to the European Union make trade easier between member countries?

questions.correctAnswer: Constitutional monarchy
questions.explanation: The United Kingdom has a monarch as head of state, but an elected Parliament makes the laws and the constitution limits the monarch's power.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A crown plus a parliament makes a constitutional monarchy.
questions.question: The United Kingdom's government includes a king or queen as head of state and an elected Parliament that makes laws. This system is a...

questions.correctAnswer: Olives, grapes, and citrus fruits
questions.explanation: The Mediterranean climate brings hot, dry summers that suit olives, grapes, and citrus, which have been grown around the sea for thousands of years.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Olives and grapes thrive on dry summer hills.
questions.question: The Mediterranean climate of southern Europe has hot, dry summers. Which famous crops grow best in it?

questions.correctAnswer: To rebuild their economies and make future wars between them less likely
distractors: To build one single European empire
Because the United States forced them to unite
To stop all trade with other continents
questions.explanation: After two world wars devastated Europe, leaders chose cooperation. Shared trade and laws rebuilt economies and tied former enemies together in peace.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Europe chose teamwork over another war.
questions.question: After World War II, why did European countries begin cooperating in organizations that eventually led to the European Union?

questions.correctAnswer: A leading maker and exporter of cars and machinery
distractors: A country with almost no industry
A country famous only for farming
questions.explanation: Germany is one of the world's top exporters. Its factories are especially known for automobiles, machinery, and engineering products.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: German factories ship cars to the world.
questions.question: In the world economy, Germany is best known as...

questions.correctAnswer: Spans two continents, Europe and Asia
distractors: Is the smallest country in Asia
Touches two oceans and nothing else
questions.explanation: Russia stretches from Eastern Europe across northern Asia to the Pacific Ocean, making it the world's largest country and a transcontinental one.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Russia is so wide it lives on two continents.
questions.question: Russia is called a transcontinental country because it...

questions.correctAnswer: The west has a milder climate and better farmland, while much of Siberia is extremely cold and harsh
distractors: The government forbids anyone from living in Siberia
Siberia is covered by the ocean
Eastern Russia has no rivers at all
questions.explanation: Most Russians live west of the Ural Mountains, where the climate is gentler. Siberia's severe cold and permafrost make large-scale settlement difficult.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Russians gather where the winters are gentler.
questions.question: Why do most Russians live in the western part of their country?

questions.correctAnswer: Their location on the Mediterranean Sea with busy ports for trade
distractors: Huge oil fields under the city of Rome
Complete isolation from all other countries
questions.explanation: Venice and other Italian city-states sat on Mediterranean trade routes. Their ships carried goods between Europe and Asia, bringing great wealth.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Venice grew rich where the trade ships sailed.
questions.question: Which feature helped Italian city-states such as Venice become wealthy trading centers long ago, shaping Italian culture today?

questions.correctAnswer: All three countries belong to the European Union, which allows citizens to move freely between member countries
distractors: Spain conquered France and Germany long ago
Europe has only one single government
questions.explanation: EU citizens have the right to live and work in any member country. France, Germany, and Spain are all EU members.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: An EU passport opens every member's door.
questions.question: A French citizen and a German citizen can both live and work in Spain without special permission mainly because...

questions.correctAnswer: The Sahara
questions.explanation: The Sahara covers most of North Africa and is the largest hot desert on Earth, nearly as big as the entire United States.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The Sahara is the king of hot deserts.
questions.question: Which is the largest hot desert in the world, covering much of North Africa?

questions.correctAnswer: It provides water for farming and daily life in an otherwise desert land
distractors: It is the world's longest mountain range
It separates Egypt from all other countries
It produces electricity for the whole world
questions.explanation: Egypt is mostly desert, but the Nile's water and floods created fertile land along its banks where farms and cities could grow.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Egypt is the gift of the Nile.
questions.question: Why has the Nile River been so important to Egypt for thousands of years?

questions.correctAnswer: Nigeria
questions.explanation: Nigeria, in West Africa, has more people than any other African country, with over 200 million residents.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Nigeria packs in more people than any African nation.
questions.question: Which African country has the largest population?

questions.correctAnswer: Oil (petroleum)
questions.explanation: Nigeria is one of the world's major oil producers, and oil sales bring in most of the government's income.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Nigeria's wealth pumps out of the ground.
questions.question: Nigeria's economy depends heavily on which natural resource?

questions.correctAnswer: It is home to thousands of ethnic groups and well over a thousand languages
distractors: Every African country speaks the same language
Only one religion is practiced there
All Africans share one single culture
